title: Horizon of a Hazard Refund Review on a Matured or Payoff-Bound Summit Loan
content:
For the kept amount of a returned hazard premium on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, the horizon of the hazard refund review is set from the Summit loan's maturity case (Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases) or payoff case (Payoff and Loan Satisfaction) where one qualifies.

1. Where the reserve's Summit loan has a maturity case that is due and payable, or in its extension period, and that case carries a resolution deadline, the horizon of the hazard refund review is the whole months from the handling date to that resolution deadline, never below zero.
2. Where it has no such maturity case and a payoff case on the loan has terms issued or accepted and carries a statement good-through date, the horizon is the whole months from the handling date to that good-through date, never below zero.
3. Where neither case qualifies, this rule does not set the horizon.

Whole months are complete calendar months, counted from the handling date; a date in the same month or earlier than one full month away gives 0.

**Hypothetical readings (handling date 20 January).**
- A maturity case in its extension period with a resolution deadline of 20 July: horizon 6 months, whatever the payoff case shows.
- A due-and-payable maturity case with no resolution deadline, and a payoff case with terms accepted and a good-through date of 19 April: horizon 2 months.
- A payoff case still open but with no terms issued or accepted: not a qualifying case.
